name: Bronzer

card.summary: A wash-off skin tint that gives an instant tanned look with no UV and no staying power.
card.aka: Body bronzer, tanning bronzer, instant tan, contour bronzer
card.note: Surface colour only: it rubs off, can streak or look orange, and gives no real sun protection.

quick.overview:
A bronzer is a cosmetic colorant, sold as a powder, lotion, gel, mousse or spray, that tints the skin until it is washed off. People use it for an instant tan look, to even out skin tone, or to add shading to the face and body.

It appears in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding circles as a quick cosmetic fix, and in bodybuilding as the colour layer used alongside spray tans on stage. It is different from a DHA self-tanner, which reacts with the skin to produce a longer-lasting colour.
quick.mechanism: Bronzers deposit colour on the outer surface of the skin. Common colourants described in encyclopedic sources include walnut extract, jojoba extract and caramel. Because the colour sits on top of the skin, it comes off with soap and water and can transfer to clothing.
quick.risks: Reported downsides are an orange or patchy look if applied unevenly, transfer onto clothing, and skin reactions in people allergic to ingredients such as fragrances or benzyl alcohol. A bronzer does not tan the skin and is not a sunscreen, and dermatology sources note that sunless products give no meaningful UV protection.

lead: A bronzer is a cosmetic product that temporarily tints the skin to look tanned. It comes as powders, lotions, gels, mousses, sprays and tinted moisturizers, and the colour lasts until it is washed off with soap and water.[1] It is often worn for a one-day tan or alongside a longer-lasting self-tanner.[1]

Unlike dihydroxyacetone (DHA) self-tanners, which react chemically with the outermost skin layer, a bronzer only coats the surface.[1] Common colourants include walnut oil extract, jojoba extract and caramel, and the product can rub off on clothing or look orange or splotchy if applied unevenly.[1] Some formulations contain potential allergens such as benzyl alcohol, tocopherol and fragrance.[1]

In looksmaxxing and fitness forums, bronzer is discussed as a quick way to add colour or facial shading, and in competitive bodybuilding it is part of stage tanning routines.[2][3] No clinical studies of bronzer as an appearance product have been published.
infobox: Powder, lotion, gel, mousse, spray, tinted moisturizer[1]
None provided by the colour itself[1]

paras: Bronzers are one branch of sunless tanning, a category that also includes DHA self-tanners, gradual tanning lotions, spray tans, tanning pills and injectable melanocortin products.[1] Encyclopedic descriptions separate bronzers from these because they act as temporary colorants rather than reacting with the skin or altering pigment.[1]

Products range from face powders used to add warmth and contouring to body lotions and sprays applied over larger areas. Tinted moisturizers and some tanning lotions also contain bronzing colour,[1] and patent filings describe a range of bronzer formulations.[4]
A bronzer deposits colour on the skin surface. Because it does not involve melanin or a chemical reaction with skin proteins, it needs no UV exposure and fades when washed or rubbed off.[1]

A DHA self-tanner, by contrast, reacts with amino acids in the dead outer layer of skin to make brown pigments over several hours, and the result lasts several days.[1] Bronzers are commonly used to give immediate colour while a DHA tan develops.[1]

No studies found. Research on tanning more generally has examined sunbeds, sun exposure and tanning addiction rather than cosmetic bronzers; a review of tanning behaviour discusses sun exposure and indoor tanning as drivers of melanoma and addictive tanning in young adults.[5]

Reported problems with bronzers are mostly cosmetic: streaking, an orange cast, and transfer to clothing and bedding.[1] Contact allergy to fragrance or preservative ingredients is possible in some products.[1]
Dermatology and cancer-prevention sources say that sunless tanning products do not protect against UV, and that a colour change from a bronzer should not be treated as sun protection.[1]

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and fitness communities
paras: Forum posters describe bronzer as a way to match facial colour to a body tan, since a body-only fake tan can leave the face looking paler.[2] Others describe using it in place of unprotected sun exposure on the face.[6]

In competitive bodybuilding discussions on T Nation, members describe stage colour as a layered process in which spray tans and bronzers are applied before a show and washed off afterwards; one poster argued that sunbed or sun tans are too light to serve as a base for the colour needed on stage.[3][7]

timeline.event: Man-Tan becomes the first commercial DHA self-tanner, the category that bronzers are often used with.[1]
Coppertone launches its DHA-based Quick Tan product.[1]

lore.intro: On T Nation and similar fitness forums, bronzer is mentioned mainly as a stage and photo tool and as a stand-in for face tanning.[2][6][7]

claims.claim: Bronzer on the face avoids the 'ghost face' left by a body-only tan
claims.believers: A poster describes bronzing the face to match a self-tan on the body after a pale face stood out in photos.[2]
claims.experts: No published studies have examined bronzer for matching facial and body colour; encyclopedic sources describe it as a temporary surface colorant.[1]

claims.claim: Bronzer is a safer substitute for sun exposure on the face
claims.believers: One member says he gets limited sun on the body but 'never on my face', and uses bronzer instead.[6]
claims.experts: Dermatology sources describe UV exposure as a major melanoma risk factor and note that bronzer itself provides no UV protection.[1][5]

claims.claim: Bodybuilders need a spray tan plus bronzer on stage because a real tan is not dark enough
claims.believers: A competitor argues that tanning beds will not get an athlete 'anywhere near as dark' as needed and that a pre-show base is pointless when stage colour is much darker.[7]
claims.experts: No published studies have examined stage tanning methods in bodybuilding.
